key_insight: Near terminal time, flow matching follows the training set’s distance geometry, with trajectories approximating exponential contraction toward the nearest sample away from Voronoi boundaries.
engineering_relevance: This geometry motivates distance-potential and path-based velocity learning, while separating initialization, velocity, contraction, and sample-allocation errors.
method: Analyze Gaussian-to-empirical flow matching using explicit nearest-sample contraction paths.
Bound trajectory and distribution errors, with Clarke subdifferentials describing limiting velocities at ties.
Learn either a distance potential with value-and-gradient supervision or velocities along contraction paths.
evidence_signal: A two-site example establishes sharpness of the general square-root Wasserstein rate, while MNIST experiments distinguish support proximity, nearest-site retention, and feature fidelity.
watch_item: Uniform trajectory guarantees exclude Voronoi interfaces, and proximity to training samples alone does not establish correct sample allocation or feature fidelity.
paper_title: Late-Time Dynamics of Flow Matching: Distance Geometry and Learning
